articles.title: Cannabis use predicts worse clinical outcomes in newly psychotic patients
articles.summary: Young adults who experience psychosis after heavy cannabis use face slower recovery times if they also battle clinical depression and hopelessness. A recent two-year study highlights how these mood states create a dangerous cycle of persistent symptoms.

articles.title: Two forms of intellectual humility have opposite links to mental health, study finds
articles.summary: New research suggests that intellectual humility relates to mental health in contrasting ways. While respecting the ideas of others is linked to greater life satisfaction, constantly questioning your own knowledge tends to be associated with anxiety.

articles.title: Fearing your own thoughts predicts worse hangover anxiety
articles.summary: Individuals who dread losing mental control are highly likely to experience severe anxiety during a hangover. New research shows this specific psychological fear reliably predicts morning-after panic, helping professionals identify young adults at risk for future alcohol problems.

articles.summary: arXiv:2607.27308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce ZUNA1.1, a 380M-parameter diffusion autoencoder for flexible EEG signal reconstruction. ZUNA1.1 is capable of reconstructing variable length sequences of up to 30s, with an arbitrary number of EEG channels at arbitrary scalp locations, and can reconstruct arbitrary temporal intervals within channels in addition to reconstructing entire channels. articles.title: Creatine supplements show potential for managing major depressive disorder
articles.summary: A new systematic review suggests that creatine monohydrate, a popular supplement for athletes, might help treat major depressive disorder. Evidence indicates that combining creatine with standard antidepressants or talk therapy tends to improve depressive symptoms in adults.

articles.title: What if the brain does not create consciousness?
articles.summary: Christof Koch is taking on one of science’s deepest mysteries: how the brain creates conscious experience, or whether it creates it at all. He argues that materialism has yet to solve this “hard problem” and will explore puzzling phenomena such as near-death experiences and terminal lucidity. His work points toward the possibility that consciousness may be woven into reality itself.

articles.title: Taking acetaminophen during pregnancy isn’t linked to autism or ADHD, new research shows
articles.summary: A massive new study reveals that taking acetaminophen during pregnancy does not increase a child’s risk of autism or ADHD. By comparing siblings, researchers found previous concerns were likely driven by shared family genetics rather than the medication.

articles.title: New study reveals an unexpected difference between casual and compulsive pornography viewers
articles.summary: A new analysis of over 100,000 individuals reveals a notable link between watching recreational pornography and engaging in interactive online sexual behaviors like sexting. The research highlights the nuanced psychological boundaries dividing casual viewing from solitary compulsive habits.

articles.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs)-powered multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed in mixed-motive environments, where agents operate under asymmetric information and strategic deception due to conflicting or hidden objectives. In these settings, misalignment with collective goals becomes a central concern. We propose a novel framework for evaluating objective misalignment using the social deduction game Werewolf, modifying the objective of a single agent while preserving its assigned role. Across LLMs from four different model families and sizes
